CHIEF COMPLAINT
Status post mitral valve repair follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 63-year-old female presenting for follow-up evaluation following mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. At previous follow-up on 9/17/2020, patient was doing well from a cardiac standpoint. She reports feeling much better since surgery and overall doing quite well. She continues to experience some chest discomfort and shallow breathing with exertion, which resolves after a few minutes with rest. Episodes occur approximately a couple times per month, lasting only a few minutes, and she has learned to modify her activity level accordingly. She reports the symptoms resolve for a couple of weeks between episodes. She is compliant with her medications, using a reminder app to help keep up with her regimen. She notes initial irritability with atenolol which has since resolved.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Chest discomfort with exertion, resolves with rest. Shallow breathing with exertion. No other new symptoms reported.

- Mitral regurgitation
- Atrial fibrillation
- Diabetes
- Asthma
- Recurrent chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease
- Status post mitral valve repair (8/3/2020)

MEDICATIONS

- Atenolol 50 mg daily

Not documented.

General: Patient appears well.
Head and Neck: No jugular venous distension detected.

Heart: Irregularly irregular rhythm consistent with atrial fibrillation. S1 slightly accentuated, no S3 gallop.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender.

RESULTS
ECG dated 12/26/2020: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, T-wave inversion anteriorly. No significant changes compared to previous study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
63-year-old female with history of mitral regurgitation and atrial fibrillation, status post mitral valve repair in 2020, presenting for follow-up. Patient is recovering well from surgery. Atrial fibrillation is well controlled on current medications. Continue current medication regimen: Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 4 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily. Encouraged to remain active as tolerated. Patient to follow up in 6-9 months. All questions answered.
